definitions: A method used in econometrics and statistics to estimate causal relationships when controlled experiments are not feasible or when there are concerns about endogeneity.

A variable that is correlated with the endogenous explanatory variable but not with the error term of the regression equation, and that affects the dependent variable only through the endogenous explanatory variable.
examples: Researchers used an instrumental variable to address the endogeneity of education in their wage regression.
The study employed an instrumental variable approach to estimate the causal effect of healthcare access.
Finding a valid instrumental variable is often the most challenging part of this econometric technique.
